question: Should the legacy `curl -fsSL https://molt.bot/install.sh | zsh` path remain supported by ClawHub/OpenClaw, or should it be retired in favor of the current bash installer and documented ClawHub/OpenClaw commands?
rationale: The failing helper is absent from current main and the live URL redirects to a hosted OpenClaw script outside this checkout, so automation cannot safely choose the support boundary or owner.

options.title: Retire legacy zsh usage
options.body: Point users at `https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash` and current ClawHub/OpenClaw install docs, then treat zsh-piped legacy failures as unsupported.

options.title: Own and harden the hosted installer
options.body: Track the installer source, reproduce the Homebrew/zsh cleanup failure, and add smoke proof for unmatched npm cleanup globs under supported shells.

options.title: Wait for fresh reporter proof
options.body: Keep the issue waiting on author until there is current evidence that a supported installer path still fails.

recommendation.title: Retire legacy zsh usage
recommendation.body: Point users at `https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash` and current ClawHub/OpenClaw install docs, then treat zsh-piped legacy failures as unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest visible owner for the maintained ClawHub CLI/package install surface and has nearby issue-triage history.
